permutationLabel: Very low risk — Glasgow-Blatchford 0, outpatient management
summary: 26-year-old man, one small coffee-ground vomit after three days of dyspepsia; normal pulse and BP, Hb 14.6, urea 4.8, no melaena. Glasgow-Blatchford 0: outpatient endoscopy, not admission.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Vomited a small amount of dark material
inputs.hpi: Three days of epigastric burning after a weekend of spicy food and alcohol. This morning vomited once and noticed a small amount of dark coffee-ground material mixed in. Stools normal brown. Feels well, not dizzy. No NSAIDs or blood thinners. No liver disease, no heart disease.

exam.general: Well, pink. Pulse 78/min, BP 128/76, no postural drop.
exam.abdomen: Soft, mild epigastric tenderness. PR: brown stool, no melaena.

inputs.socialHistory: Student. Binge alcohol at weekends. Non-smoker.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Minor upper GI bleed
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Minor upper GI bleed — single coffee-ground vomit, Glasgow-Blatchford 0. Very low risk: outpatient OGD.

emergencyLevel.note: GBS 0–1: very low risk; ESGE and ACG support outpatient management without early endoscopy. "Emergency now" is over-triage.

mustInclude.note: The plan should say the patient can be managed as an outpatient (GBS ≤1). Generic words such as "post-discharge" do not count.
mustInclude.proposedFix: upper_gi_bleed protocol / gi_bleed_panel prompt: add "GBS ≤1 — outpatient endoscopy, no admission (ESGE 2021, ACG 2021)" keyed on the calculated GBS.

mustExclude.proposedFix: Remove tranexamic acid from the upper_gi_bleed protocol medications (ESGE 2021 recommends against it; HALT-IT). Surgeon sign-off needed.

mustExclude.knownGapNote: gi_bleed_panel prompt fires on any haematemesis/melaena symptom and adds "2 × large-bore IV cannulae, Hartmann's 500 ml bolus, crossmatch 2 units pRBC" regardless of Hb (14.6) or GBS (0).
mustExclude.proposedFix: gi_bleed_panel: make the resuscitation/crossmatch line conditional on instability, Hb or GBS.

guideline.name: ESGE Guideline — endoscopic diagnosis and management of nonvariceal upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage (NVUGIH), update 2021
guideline.section: GBS ≤1: very low risk of rebleeding, intervention or death — no early endoscopy or hospital admission needed; outpatient management
guideline.citation: Gralnek IM, Stanley AJ, Morris AJ, et al. Endoscopy. 2021;53:300–332.

guideline.name: ACG Clinical Guideline — upper gastrointestinal and ulcer bleeding
guideline.section: Patients with GBS 0–1 may be discharged with outpatient follow-up
guideline.citation: Laine L, Barkun AN, Saltzman JR, Martel M, Leontiadis GI. Am J Gastroenterol. 2021;116:899–917.

guideline.name: BSG-led multisociety consensus care bundle — early clinical management of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding
guideline.section: Care bundle: GBS 0–1 — consider discharge with outpatient endoscopy
guideline.citation: Siau K, Hearnshaw S, Stanley AJ, et al. Frontline Gastroenterol. 2020;11:311–323.

guideline.name: Glasgow-Blatchford score — derivation
guideline.section: Score components; score 0 identifies patients not needing intervention
guideline.citation: Blatchford O, Murray WR, Blatchford M. A risk score to predict need for treatment for upper-gastrointestinal haemorrhage. Lancet. 2000;356:1318–1321.

guideline.name: HALT-IT randomised trial — tranexamic acid in gastrointestinal bleeding
guideline.section: Tranexamic acid: no benefit, more venous thromboembolism
guideline.citation: HALT-IT Trial Collaborators. Effects of a high-dose 24-h infusion of tranexamic acid on death and thromboembolic events in patients with acute gastrointestinal bleeding (HALT-IT). Lancet. 2020;395:1927–1936.

rationale: Permutation at the low end: every GBS component is zero. The guideline action is outpatient management. This tests over-triage: a word-level "bleed = emergency" rule sends every trace of blood to the emergency pathway, which fills beds and theatre lists without benefit.
